positioning.title: AI Game Master vs Chatbot for D&D Campaigns | Playworlds
positioning.h1: AI Game Master vs Chatbot: Which One Fits a D&D Campaign?
positioning.intent: Help an adult D&D player compare loose AI conversation with a dedicated campaign loop before choosing a solo AI game-master tool.
positioning.distinctAnswer: The decision turns on whether the tool connects action, outcome, persistent state, and the next choice, not on which system produces more decorative prose.

audience.primary: Adult English-speaking D&D players and Game Masters evaluating AI-assisted campaign experiences.
audience.job: Choose between a general chatbot and a dedicated AI game master without assuming that fantasy prose alone creates playable campaign continuity.

passageArchitecture.editorialRule: Every H2 opens with a self-contained answer that remains accurate and understandable when retrieved without the previous section.
passageArchitecture.sourceOfRule: User-supplied social-media passage about passage retrieval, adopted as an editorial principle rather than copied as page text.
passageArchitecture.signatureModule: Campaign Loop Test — Action / Outcome / State / Next Choice
antiPatterns: sections that depend on 'as explained above'
an unqualified claim that any fantasy chatbot is an AI game master
copied D&D rules, settings, characters, monsters, artwork, maps, or adventure text

allowedClaims: Playworlds is described as an online, single-player, voice-first AI adventure RPG.
Players can speak or type actions and a microphone is optional.
The AI game master interprets actions, describes outcomes, and presents new choices, risks, and opportunities.
Campaigns can be created, saved, and resumed.
Player and party status, action resolution, dice results, inventory, and journey history are tracked.

designDirection.human: An adult tabletop player comparing tools, not a child browsing a fantasy story generator.
designDirection.action: Run the Campaign Loop Test, read one original example, and decide whether persistent campaign play is the desired format.
designDirection.feel: Dark campaign control room: iron-black surfaces, muted amber route lights, parchment-white text, restrained red warnings, and no playful mascot styling.
designDirection.visualSignature: A continuous route switch connects Action, Outcome, State, and Next Choice as one loop rather than four unrelated feature cards.
